text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwait's Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah discusses mutual ties with Sri Lanka's President Kumaratunga.
- Defence Minister Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah starts official visit to Britain.
- Britain under Labour rule seen giving Gulf region special importance.
- Kuwait, Hungary discuss cooperation in fighting narcotics.
- State subsidies allocated to domestic industries amounted to 23 million dinars ($76 million) in past four years, Minister of Trade and Industry Mudaf says.
- Government promises to present parliament with bill that would justify drafts from state reserves, parliamentarian says.
- Turkey could be planning to create 450 km (280 mile)-long security zone on Iraq's border with Iran, Syria and Turkey.
- U.N. official in charge of inspecting Iraq's mass destruction weapons, Rolf Ekeus, to visit Iraq in June.
- Judicial council expected to probe four prosecutors on alleged bribe charges.
- Kuwait, Red Cross discuss POWs issue. Kuwait says Iraq still detains some 600 Kuwaitis since 1990-91 Iraqi occupation of Gulf Arab state. Iraq denies this.
